title: Disaster Recovery Primer
scenario: Welcome to Disaster Recovery Primer. Before proceeding, you must master these essential networking terms. Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF): Average time between hardware failures. Higher = more reliable. Used to calculate availability: MTBF / (MTBF + MTTR). Key metric for hardware procurement and HA design. Mean Time To Repair (MTTR): Average time to restore a failed component. Lower = faster recovery. Availability = MTBF / (MTBF + MTTR). Drives sparing strategy and support contract SLAs. Recovery Time Objective (RTO): Maximum acceptable downtime after a disaster — how quickly must systems be restored? Business defines this. Drives DR site type: hot (minutes), warm (hours), cold (days/weeks). Recovery Point Objective (RPO): Maximum acceptable data loss measured in time — how old can the recovered data be? RPO of 1hr means backups every hour. Drives backup frequency and replication strategy.
question: What does MTBF stand for?
explanation: MTBF stands for Mean Time Between Failures.
